script: What is your typical morning routine like when you're getting ready for work, and how do you usually decide what to eat for lunch?
Can you tell me about a recent time when you had to order food from someone else to bring into the office - was it convenient or inconvenient, and why did you choose that option?

How much would you be willing to pay for a hot, home-style meal delivered to your office before 10am, and are there any specific features or benefits that would make you more or less likely to order from this ghost kitchen?
interview_answers:
My mornings are pretty hectic, to be honest. I wake up around 6:30 am, get dressed in the dark, and rush to get some breakfast before leaving for work. Usually, it's something simple like a bowl of cereal or toast with tea. If I have time, I'll make myself an egg sandwich or scramble some eggs - nothing too fancy.

As for lunch, I rely heavily on WhatsApp to order food from this new ghost kitchen that just opened up in Lagos. They claim to deliver Nigerian home-style lunches, which sounds amazing to me. But, to be honest, their menu is a bit limited and inconsistent. Sometimes they have jollof rice or egusi soup, but not always. I'll send them a message saying "I'd like to order lunch for delivery" and then they'll ask what I want. If they don't have it, I'm stuck with something else.

It's frustrating because sometimes I get hung up on the website, waiting for my order, and by the time it arrives, I've already gotten hungry again. And if there are issues with the order or delivery, I just end up dealing with that instead of enjoying my lunch.

I think the last time I ordered food through this ghost kitchen was like two days ago. It was a pretty typical morning for me, rushing around trying to get everything done before my shift started at the office.

I sent them a message saying "I'd like to order lunch for delivery" and they asked what I wanted. I told them I was in the mood for something spicy, so they recommended their jollof rice with egusi soup. It sounded good, so I went with it.

The only issue was that my phone kept losing signal in the office building, so I had to wait a bit longer than expected for the message to confirm my order. When it finally did, I got an estimated time of delivery, but then when they arrived, there were some issues with the order - they'd run out of egusi soup.

It was pretty frustrating because I was already running late for work and now I had to deal with this extra hassle. But at the same time, having food delivered to my office can be really convenient, especially on busy days when I don't have much time to spare.

I guess what I would say is that while ordering from the ghost kitchen works out sometimes, it's not always reliable or convenient for me. Sometimes they're out of certain dishes, and the delivery times are sketchy...

To be honest, I'm not really sure how much I'd be willing to pay for a hot, home-style meal delivered to my office before 10am. My budget is pretty tight, and I try to stick to what I can afford.

If they could offer something that's reliable and consistent, with a wide range of menu options, maybe I'd be more willing to pay a bit more. But if it's just going to be hit-or-miss, or if the prices are too high, then I'm not sure I'd be interested.

Actually, the fact that they're out of egusi soup sometimes is a big turn-off for me. If they could guarantee that certain dishes would always be available, that would be really appealing. And having options like jollof rice and egusi soup being the usual suspects would make me more likely to order from them.

But if they had some kind of limited-time offer or promotion that included free delivery or a discount, maybe I'd be more willing to give it another try. I haven't thought about that much, but usually I'd probably just stick with what I know and trust.
